title: Exploring FlyBase Data Using QuickSearch
author: Marygold
materials: Computer or other device with access to the internet
An up‐to‐date web browser, such as Firefox, Chrome, or Safari, with JavaScript and cookies enabled

steps.title: Prepare computer and browser
steps.instruction: Ensure you have a computer or other device with internet access and an up‑to‑date web browser (Firefox, Chrome, or Safari) with JavaScript and cookies enabled.

steps.title: Choose appropriate QuickSearch tab
steps.instruction: Select the QuickSearch tab that matches your query: “Search FlyBase” for a broad, case‑insensitive search of all FlyBase data classes and ontologies; “Data Class” to restrict the query to a single data class or ontology; “Gene Groups”, “Pathways”, “GO”, “Protein Domains”, “Expression”, “GAL4 etc”, “Phenotype”, “Human Disease”, or “Homologs” for specialized searches.

steps.title: Enter a valid search term
steps.instruction: In the chosen tab, type the official current name, symbol, or ID of the entity you are interested in. Use the autocomplete feature (available in all tabs except the general “Search FlyBase” tab) to confirm validity. If the term is not recognized, first search it in the “Search FlyBase” tab with the “Everything” option selected, locate the correct term, or use the Vocabularies tool.

steps.title: Add wildcard if needed
steps.instruction: Append, prepend, or insert an asterisk (*) to your search term to broaden the query. Wildcards are not supported in the Expression, GAL4 etc, Phenotype, and Homologs tabs.

steps.title: Review and manage hit list
steps.instruction: After the query, examine the returned hit list. Use the “View as” control to switch between the default “List” view and the “Table” view (available when results comprise a single data class). In Table view, sort columns as needed. For single‑class hit lists, you may also click the “Convert”, “Export”, or “Analyze” buttons to further process the data.

steps.title: Access tab‑specific help
steps.instruction: Click the “?” icon within any QuickSearch tab to open the online help documentation for that tab.

steps.title: Troubleshoot common problems
steps.instruction: If the search fails or returns unexpected results, consult Table 4 for common problems and suggested solutions, or use the “Contact FlyBase” link at the bottom of every FlyBase page to request assistance, report a bug, or suggest a new feature.

steps.title: Interpret and document results
steps.instruction: Record the FlyBase release number shown in the page header/footer. Click individual hits to view their detailed report pages and examine original data sources before drawing conclusions. Remember that broad searches may yield false positives while overly restrictive searches may miss relevant data; iterative refinement of the query is often required.
